text_fidelity_a:
Clement Cycling Strada LGG Clincher 120 TPI Tire I recently bought a new Specialized Sirrus hybrid bicycle. Toady I swapped out the OEM tires and tubes for Clement Cycling Strada LGG 120 TPI 700cx28 clincher tires and Continental MTB/Race 28 700x25-32 tubes with 60mm Presta valves. The LGG tires weigh 233g each (my actual measurements), compared to 478g for the stock Espoir Sport Reflect 700x30c tires. The width of the LGG's on the stock 26mm (outside width) rims is 29.8mm, compared to 32.4mm for the stock tires. The Conti tubes weigh 140g, compared to 154g for the stock tubes. The overall weight savings was a surprising 259g, or 9.14oz, for each wheel.

Riding at the same tire pressure, 70 lbs front and 75 lbs back, the LGG tires had much quicker handling and the ride felt more cushioned. The more cushioned ride may be due to the heavy, relatively stiff carcass on the stock tires compared to the very lightweight and flexible sidewalls on the LGGs.
text_fidelity_b: Clement Cycling Strada LGG Clincher 120 TPI Tire

text_fidelity_a:
Sevylor Tahiti Professional Self Bailing kayak We bought this kayak a year ago & used it heavily last summer. I'm amazed at how it has performed. It has a permanent place in our RV. It isn't as bulky as the Sea Eagle Paddle Ski we have & is easier to get to the water. My husband used it for exercise about every other day. I LOVE fishing from it. You can paddle into the tightest & shallowest places to fish & you're sitting (or kneeling) right in the water without getting wet. I would fish for hours comfortably. I would let a large rock in the water hold the boat steady while I fished a spot & not see wear-marks on the hull afterwards, so it became a regular fishing strategy. Especially effective is drifting with the current with a line out. Make sure you carry a large net if you're going to fish from it. I used to carry a one-hand net until I caught a 40" Northern Pike from it. Now I take a pole net.

That's another advantage in using it for fishing. When I realized I had something larger than a bass on my hook, I let out the drag & let it pull me around in the kayak. What a hoot! About 5 minutes later, I saw it was a Pike.

It is also very stable & fun to cross large wakes in. I admit I'm disturbed when in our hard-sided boat, other boats rock ours with large wakes. In the Tahiti I love seeing a wake come my way.

The Tahiti moves easily in the water. We put a skeg on it, which I recommend. It made a difference in tracking. If our boat wears out, we will definitely get another Tahiti. We've already gotten our money's worth out of this one.
text_fidelity_b: Sevylor Tahiti Professional Self Bailing kayak

text_fidelity_a:
Augason Farms Freeze Dried Sweet Corn 16 oz #10 Can Big fan of prepping for emergencies and whatever else that may impact food supplies. I buy from Augason Farms regularly. I have never had any major issues or concerns with any of their products. Sellers yes, products no. I buy emergency food and tuck it away. I try to buy when on sale because I am basically buying food and not eating it. I rarely get into it, or rotate it. If I am buying from Augason farms, then the packaging is just fine for super long term storage (10-25 years depending on the food item). I get the occasional dented can (this one was fine), and it makes no impact. It isnt like other food grade cans where the can is breeched. These cans are made to withstand floods and other crazy stuff. They float, did you know that? Sometimes I will get into a can early if I bought it on sale and it is same price or cheaper than non long term storage equivalent (recently I experienced that with powdered butter. My usual bagged brand was more expensive than the sale price of Augason powdered butter.. stuff like that).

Anyway, I like the corn to be consumed as is, tossed in a big bowl of salad, or rehydrated when used in soups or as a side. Not my number one prep item, but it does add variety.

Occasionally I see people post reviews that say they got an expired product. But they never show a picture of the date they are looking at. The cans show the manufacture date first and foremost, then follows the best by date many many many years in the future. If they got an expired product, then do the math. That means the product would have been made 10-25 years ago. I mean, maybe. Lets see the label. They change the look of their label on occasion. So anyway, I am always suspect of those reviews. I just think they arent reading it right, and if it was legit they would post a pic of the can.
text_fidelity_b: Augason Farms Freeze Dried Sweet Corn 16 oz #10 Can

The box included 4 CR123a batteries. You only need 2 for powering the light. Putting the batteries in place takes some talent by aligning the cover back to the base while the batteries are pressing against it. It is just a bit tricky but the cover will snap in place while holding with one hand and you can snap the lock with the other hand. The on/off switch in my opinion is in a good location. I also like that it stays out of the way from your finger until you need it.

Also the flashlight comes with additional clips for mounting it on a Picatinnny rail. The use of the clips will depend on what kind of hunting item you will be using it on. The stock one that came installed worked for me. They are easy to change out by removing a screw on the flashlight side. The included clips may also allow for how close you want the on /off switch to your finger.

Final thoughts: I like this brand and model. I also feel it is in a fair price range. The light is bright and should last a long time before having to replace the batteries. One more note is that to replace batteries, the flashlight will need to be taken off the Picatinny rail. I am giving this Feyachi flashlight 5 stars for good quality construction, value and brightness.

text_fidelity_a: Solo Stove Pot 1800 Stainless Steel Companion Pot great Cookware for Backpacking Camping Survival Backpacking Kitchen and Cooking simple Equipment Set & Accessories for Hiking Campfires and Adventure The Solo Stove Titan and Solo Pot 1800 is the perfect pairing of fit, functionality and form! Once again the makers have outdone themselves. The Solo Stove Titan in it's nylon bag nests perfectly inside the Solo Pot 1800. The stove and pot are both sturdily constructed of beautiful stainless steel. For my test burn it was already dark and chilly by the time I arrived at my test camp site, so I opted for using my Trangia alcohol burner inside of the Titan instead of foraging for sticks and kindling. After getting the alcohol lit and up to full burn, I placed 20oz of water exactly (I know thanks to the handy imprinted measuring lines built into the pot) on the stove and set my timer. At 4 minutes, I had surface bubbles forming at the bottom of the pot. At 6 minutes I saw some rolling bubbles and had a lot of vapor filling the chilly air when I lifted the lid by it's silicone coated lid tab. At 8 minutes I had a full boil and removed the pot from the fire by its cool fold out handles. This winning combo is going to be my go to camp cooking kit. I love it and highly recommend it!

The first thing I noticed was the fly is very thin material, unlike my 10 yr old Field and Stream.  While carefully inspecting the fly I noticed a small tear, although it was carefully opened .  The winds picked up during our visit and unfortunately I faced the opening into the wind.  It is really noisy.  Drove to the Keys and had a big rainstorm. text_fidelity_a:
Plano Stowaway Micro Organizer Premium Tackle Organization I don't know why everybody is having problems with these 3214 boxes. I've been using them for years - at least 10 years - the brownish kind that's labeled "Micro Mag". I've never had a single problem with them and I prefer them over the 3414 soft plastic white ones, although these are slightly heavier than the 3414's. When I want to just carry one little kit in my vest or pocket, these are perfect. I've accidentally dropped them on hard surfaces without any breakage or cracks. Of course, I'm sure there's a limit to how much abuse they will take, but if you're careful with your fishing gear there should be no problem.

Since I gave two of them away to my son and wife, I needed a replacement. I tried to consolidate all of my trout gear into one, but found I could be a little more organized with two. I use one for all my terminal tackle, hooks and weights (separated by size) and I'll use the other one for all my lures. The problem I have with the white 3414 box is that the lids don't seal tightly. Every one I've ever had or inspected on the shelf has the same issue. The lids are slightly bowed out. So, when you put a bunch of tiny #14 hooks, swivels, and the like, they always end up migrating to another section. Really irritating. That NEVER happens with the hard 3214.

When I saw these green ones (I've never seen them in the stores), I thought it was perfect. I like the color and it differentiates between my brown one. Comparing it to my old brown one, it is exactly the same - except mine is not labeled Micro Mag like in the picture. The top is just kind of plain with a small Plano logo. text_fidelity_a:
Viper by GLD Products 800 Regulation Size Electronic Dartboard, Featuring 57 Game options for up to 16 players, Enhanced Scoring Experience with Ultra-Thin Spider, and Top Quality Segments to Reduce Bounce Outs, Black I was pleasantly surprised at how well this dartboard works and how many different game options it offers. I am old school and prefer to just play the basic game but, the kids all love playing all the other game options this board offers. Keeps them busy and entertained for hours.
Can either play against the computer for a lot of practice or you can play against other players.
First observation is the darts. They're nice and light so they don't do any damage to my walls if a wild dart is thrown. They're cheap and will break but you can easily replace these, if they do break. I like keeping the cheaper darts out for the kids to play with. The darts are held right onto the board so there's no searching around for them. Not saying the kids will put the darts in the right spot when done playing but, it's a nice convenience. You can also upgrade your darts to the heavier more expensive ones they sell. Warning, the heavier darts will put marks on the walls. So the better ones I keep in a case and are only used by my wife and I. The heavier ones do stick into the board a lot tighter. Best to just twist dart back and forth, like a screwdriver, and then pull it out. Haven't had any problem with my better darts breaking so far.
The game board is really well made. No problems with the darts holding in the small holes. Scoring is spot on so no issues with that at all.
I was worried about the LCD screen being hit by any darts. Especially the heavier ones I have. So, I took a thin piece of plexiglass, cut it down to the size I wanted, and attached it over the LCD display to protect it. I have multiple yoga mats; I tend to select different ones for different uses. The one I rely on the most is my [[ASIN:B00AB3LLVS Manduka eKO Lite Yoga Mat]], as it is lightweight, thin (which I prefer), and the most dependably non-slip mat I have ever tried.

This Kharma Khare mat is slightly thicker than my Manduka eKo Lite. However, unlike some thick yoga mats, it is not a squishy thickness, which I can't stand--rather, it is nice and firm, and it feels great under your feet. Standing on the mat, I got great grip and felt that the mat was very secure. When my hands were on the mat--in downward dog, for example--I thought that the grip was decent, but not QUITE as good as with my eKo mat. Still, overall I feel confident practicing yoga on this mat.

To me, the main selling point of the Kharma Khare mat is that it is made from recycled tires--love this! Mine did have a bit of a rubbery odor when I first unrolled it, but this dissipated after I 1) wiped it down with the included yoga mat wipes (not sure if this is standard, but I received 20 2-packs of these), and 2) left it unrolled for several days. The only other (minor) negative of this mat is that the black color easily shows dusty footprints; I noticed this more using this mat than with any of my other mats. Still, I would highly recommend this mat, especially for the eco-conscious yogi, and my final rating is 4 1/2 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Kharma Khare Reincarnated Lite Non Slip Eco-Friendly Yoga Mat - 4 Mm (Black)

Exercise fitness sliders Dual Sided sliding discs for Gliding Discs Exercise to Enhance Coordination of Whole Body,Abdominal Exercise Equipment,Perfect for Carpet or Hardwood Floors (Black) As I started to exercise at home more, I decided that gllders/slider may be a good and affordable option to add to my exercise routine. As I have used gliders in the past at gyms, I decided these may be a good option since it was advertised to be able to use on different types of surfaces.

The sliders are a hard plastic on one side and a cushion on the flip side. You have to be careful as you need to use the cushion surface side down when using on wood floors whereas use plastic side down on most other surfaces. I tried them on artificial grass, carpeting, and wood floors. On carpeting/rugs, they work great. They slide pretty easily. They don't glide as well on other surfaces. On the turf, they barely worked and on wood floors, they worked marginally better, but not great. If you use the sliders in the wrong direction on wood floors, the plastic will likely scratch.

Note that the size of the gliders are 7 inches in diameter, which may be a tad small for men with larger hands. For using with your feet, they should work fine for most individuals.

Bottom line - they are low cost additions for home workouts, but I would only recommend if you are going to use on carpeting or a rug.

text_fidelity_a:
Lifetime 90421 Pickleball, Paddle Badminton, & Quickstart Tennis Net Set This is a well designed, easy to break down and store game set. It's definitely geared more towards families and young kids moreso than older teens or hardcore gamers. I say this because pickleball and "quickstart tennis" won't keep older kids occupied for too long. Badminton might: the net can be set to the correct height of 61" for badminton, but you should probably get some different racquets for that. Unfortunately, the net is not the correct width and cannot easily be converted to the correct height for regular tennis.

That is, in fact, one of my two disappointments about the set. The poles are the nice coated metal type that shouldn't rust if you keep them from getting too scratched up, and they have easy set up holes for setting the net height, BUT the holes are only at 36" and 61". It would have been easy to add a few more options.

The other complaint is that the plastic bases cannot fit in the long carry bag with the poles - the opening is slightly too small. This also seems like it would have been an easy fix. That said, it's still easy to break down and store away, having just a bag for the four poles, a bag for the racquets and balls/birdies, and two handled bases that one can keep full of sand or empty of water with each use (sand is recommended, but concrete mix will work as well) and stack on top of each other. They also have caps for the filling holes.

The included racquets are the painted plywood with attached handles type that you might get with a table tennis set, only larger. They're fine, and it doesn't make much sense to include something more expensive, because if you want something more expensive you probably want to pick it out to your specifications.

Overall I like it pretty much. It doesn't take much time to set up or take down so that shouldn't stop people from playing if they so desire. It doesn't take much room to store, either, so it won't be a problem to keep in a basement or garage without getting in the way.
text_fidelity_b: Lifetime 90421 Pickleball, Paddle Badminton, & Quickstart Tennis Net Set

text_fidelity_a:
AmazonCommercial Rotomolded Coolers, 45 Quart Towable, White 20 quart Capacity:

I was hoping for mobile cooler that would be good for holding a decent amount of food or drinks. The cooler is very durable and robust. It is sturdy enough for someone to stand on without even deflecting the lid. The seal between the top of the cooler and the main compartment is tight. The hinges are molded out of the rotomolded plastic. It also has rubber feet. This reminds me of the type of cooler that would be used to transport organs by a hospital - very high quality with no doubt that it will keep the products inside cool for a long period of time.

Unfortunately, it did not satisfy my needs. I didn't realize how small the interior capacity would be. The exterior dimensions of the cooler are 12 inch deep x 19-1/2 inches and the inside dimensions are 8 inches x 14--1/2. That means the cooler is 4-5 inches thick at some locations, which is obvious by the heavy weight of the cooler. With nothing inside, the cooler weighs around 17 pounds, which doesn't sound like much, but it is relatively heavy for what you would expect for a cooler of this size and capacity.

The other thing that I don't love is the big 'amazon commercial' yellow sticker on the front that sticks out like a sore thumb. Of course, they need to market their product, but they could have added branding in a more subtle way.

45 quart Capacity:
The 45 quart capacity has all the same features and attributes as the 20 quart, but just a little larger and heavier. I think this one is versatile and functional.
Exterior Dimensions: 27 inches x 15-1/4 inch
Interior Dimensions: 21-1/2 x 11 in
Empty Weight: 26-1/2 lb

text_fidelity_a:
Concept2 Model D Indoor Rowing Machine (Gray) This review is coming from a dumpy middle-aged woman with a hip replacement who *thought* she was going to buy a treadmill. I started comparison shopping for treadmills even though spending $1000 or more on a machine instead of just going outside for a walk seemed kind of ridiculous, even in the snow. Then I ran across an article that mentioned rowing machines as the best overall piece of home exercise equipment. Some of my college dorm mates rowed on the women's 8 and it was like the light went on. The unanimous glowing reviews for the Concept2 Model D sold me on this machine and I ordered it direct from Concept2.

After about a month I can recommend rowing without reservation. The machine itself is built like a tank. It took about 20 minutes to put it together and about 2 minutes to figure out how to separate the parts for storage. It takes about 20 seconds to actually pull the machine apart and tuck it away in a corner when I'm not using it, which I do every day. Separated, it takes up the floor space of a medium-sized refrigerator. Together, it's about 9 feet long and a possible trip hazard. I use it on a carpeted floor and haven't noticed any problems with slipping and the machine doesn't need to be leveled. Gunk tends to accumulate on the rollers under the seat, which would probably go unnoticed if you don't pull the sled off and tip it up, but it's easy to clean.

I spent the first week focusing on correct technique and not killing myself. The machine comes with two booklets, a memory card, and a bottle of chain oil. The Indoor Rowing booklet has a lot of good information on proper form and suggested workouts starting from your very first day. There are also videos and active user forums on the Concept2 website. I've been following the suggestions, started slowly, set the damper at 3 and have left it there. Most nights I row from 25 to 40 minutes followed by stretching (recommended: AM/PM Stretch with Madeleine Lewis or AM Yoga for Your Week with Rodney Yee). I spent a lot of time on form and kept my stroke rate at about 18-19 spm. Slow, right? But I don't get sloppy and as I get stronger it seems that upping the stroke rate doesn't really improve my performance all that much. Before I started rowing, the morning routine was to get out of bed with cramping in my thigh and buttocks that nearly put me in tears. No joke: this disappeared overnight as soon as I started rowing. I felt a little soreness, mostly in my upper back, but zero lower back pain and no cramping AT ALL. One week of this was worth the $900.

The rowing machine puts you in total control of your workout in terms of how hard and how fast you want to work, and doesn't require you to do anything other than row harder or faster - there's no incline or speed buttons to push like with a treadmill. The rowing motion feels quite natural to me and time slides by. I actually look forward to my rowing time, and even though I'm still just getting started there is nothing about this that makes me feel like I won't be looking forward to my rowing time any less by next year. VIVITORY Adjustable Dumbbell Weight Set, 1 Pair 11/20/28/37 Lbs Dumbbell Set with Non-Slip Neoprene Handles, All-Purpose Men Exercise Dumbbells Set for Home Gym Office Workout Fitness Strength building is part of many exercise routines. To build muscle, you need to lift weights or otherwise add weight to your body in some way. Dumbbells are a good way to accomplish this and a good option for those who want to lift their weight is this set of Adjustable Dumbbells, from Vivitory.

I’ve used many dumbbells in my day, but this is the first time I have ever had a set that was adjustable. You adjust the weight by removing or adding steel bars and by doing this, you can reduce the weight down to about 5.5 pounds each or even less if you leave off the caps. The maximum weight for each dumbbell is about 18 pounds with all the rods in place. This is enough weight range to make these dumbbells using for many strength- building routines.

Removing and adding the weights to these dumbbells takes time, so don’t go into this thinking it’s going to be quick and simple. It will take effort, but it’s still simple enough that most people wont mind. The reason it takes some effort is because you also have to make sure the pads are in place, otherwise the steel rods will move around while you do your workout.

These dumbbells are easy to grip and they look better than traditional dumbbells, which feature free weights. The colorful appearance is cool, not that this means much for working out, but it does look nicer, less industrial/rugged than the traditional style. And the bars hold in place well- you don’t need to worry that they will fall out while you use the dumbbells.

Strength building is important to those who exercise. A good set of dumbbells can make strength building easier and If you’re the type who doesn’t want to mess with free weights, you might consider this dumbbell set from Vivitory. It’s a good set for those who want a single set of dumbbells for their workout routine.

My wife thought I was being a bit foolish, but she doesn’t think that anymore! In fact, this Portable Telescopic Stool has only been in the house a bit over 24 hours and we’ve used it half a dozen times! I came up with the idea of a stool when she was nursing her broken foot - it was 5+ months of bed and my needing to help her rehab it - often finding myself kneeling on our floor, which has very hard cement under the carpet - without a carpet pad - so I was hurting. Then there are any number of times one of us ended up needing a stool... but ended up kneeling on the floor or sitting not the floor... So it arrived yesterday and we popped it open - it is really easy. Fingers in the two holes on either end, twist, and pull, twist a little back and it locks in place. We wanted to test the weight - I am a bit heavy still - so I sat on it first. Held me absolute fine. Felt sturdy and safe. But we wanted to really test it - again, I’m a bit heavy right now, so we set it up next to the bed and she stop by me - in case anything went wrong I’d throw myself onto the bed - and up I went - I stood my 200+ body weight on the stool and it worked fine. it stayed in place. I will add: earlier today my wife sat on it for about 20 minutes and did note that it was starting to get a bit uncomfortable. There is no padding - just the plastic - so after awhile she was feeling it. You might be able to rig something to make it more comfortable. But for shorter periods of time it’s fine. Longer and we’ll figure something out - I hope. But overall we are both surprised and thrilled with this Portable Telescopic Stool. It’ll give us the quick stool we’ve needed, and for longer needs, well... we’ll figure something out. But so far, it’s already made a big difference.

text_fidelity_a:
Black Diamond Distance FL Trekking Pole I love these poles with the exception of a few minor things.

I love how quickly i can 'fold' these up without losing my length setting. And I love how short they fold up, and I can put them under the compression straps of my day pack. They will even fit inside if need be. Swing weight is very lite and I have had zero issue with slipping. I love the little rubber tips, which are replacable if/when they wear out. I also like the minimal baskets to allow the sections to clip together.

The few things I wish were better
The straps are fiddly to adjust and are not particularly comfortable, but not enough to be a true negative. I wish the straps had the traditional 1/2 twist rather than the method they use to have the strap lay flat under your hand. While it works, I futz with it a lot. I hope the strap issue are minimized as I use them more and strap conform to my hands better.
The handle is a little bit small and I don't have particularly large hands. Could be an issue for people with larger hands. While not really an issue for me, I plan to wrap some tennis grip around the handle.
I wish the handle had a 'trigger'.

They click a bit when using them. But I guess that is the price to pay for the quick/short break down capability. It's not a big issue but they are not as silent as say the REI carbon fiber poles, which I didn't like for various reasons but they were dead silent and had super comfy straps from day one. But that straps were even worse to adjust.

I'm really happy with these, especially for the price. As you can see the negatives were not enough for me to knock them down a star.

Sunny Sports got them out when they said they would, next day since I ordered too late for same day, And UPS as usual put them on a Donkey train, and they got there on the very last day of the expected delivery date. Since I ordered a weekend and the 5 days deliver time put them over another weekend It took 10 days. But that is not Sunny Sports fault.
text_fidelity_b: Black Diamond Distance FL Trekking Pole

text_fidelity_a:
Cateye HL-1500 Gray Silver Halogen Headlight My review on HL 1500 is comparison against other models in this category which is, single unit(meaning no wire, no separate battery compartment), operates on regular batteries. If you are looking for a comparison to other type, specially high end models costing hundreds, this won't help.
Other models I had tried and some of them still in use are, Cateye HL500(2xC), Cateye EL500II MicroHalogen(4xAA), PlanetBike Super Spot 1W LED(4xAA). HL 500 and SuperShot are no longer in use because of not enough output. Super Spot 1W uses good plastic and good mechanical design, I wish it had more brightness. This made me convinced that LED stil has a long way to go, so I won't be trying another anytime soon.

Here's my review on HL 1500, mostly against MicroHalogen(HL500II).

Pros;
* Good illumination for its class about the same as HL500II Micro Halogen but has better pattern. 1W LED comes no where near this when it come to output. HL 1500 has wider(but not by much) more even with less waste outside area.
* It doesn't make ruttling noise as HL500II does while the bike is picking up the bumps. Sheets of sponge inside are probably helping the battery in place.
* Inexpensive, but I would pay a little more for the better material and construction.
* It works reasonably long time at more than 3 hrs per charge of NiMH. Since this is marketed mostly for commuting rider, 3 hrs. one way trip is highly unlikely. It's not marketed for 24 hr. race. If you know you are going to be riding in the dark more than 3 hrs. you can always carry a spare set of batteries or spare unit with batteies installed.
* It has two settings, high and low, where HL500II has only one which is the same as high on HL1500. Low setting maybe useful when riding in the city where you don't need much light but you need the drivers to know where you are.

Cons;
* It uses cheap plastic, all Cateye I had the same. It specially affects HL500II because the plastic parts are holding together against each other, this causes more stress to the plastic. On the other hand, HL1500 uses screw to hold the two plastic parts together. My HL500II already has cracks and about to come apart. Super Spot had thinner yet stronger plastic shell.
* It's bigger than HL500II. Not much of a problem but the space on the handle bar is limited. Smaller, the better.
* Not resistant to weather element, neither HL500II. HL1500 has only one rubber parts around the reflector housing, that's it.
* Replacing battery is not easy. You'll need a coin to screw and unscrew and the screw is hard to catch the nut at the other end. I wouldn't want to do it in the dark. Maybe better to have another unit with battery in, since it's not that expensive. On the other hand, HL500II doesn't use screw. It's going to be still hard in the dark but not as much as HL1500.

At the end, I prefer HL1500 over HL500II. I'm thinking getting another one, or maybe two.

*update*(Jan-15-10)
I ordered two more, this time from BikeWorldUSA(through Amazon but no longer available). It cost me less than $20.- for 2 units and shipping, can't beat the price. I got my first one from Cambria Bicycle Outlet. It's nice to have a spare unit with batteries already installed. My next question still remains, how long it'll take for the bulb to burn out.
I put a flat washer between the screw and the plastic body. There's nothing stopping the screw from chewing up the plastic.

*update*(Dec-22-10)
I took the HL-1500 to local bike shop and asked them to let me compare the brightness against other models, which they kindly accepted. Against EL-500(Cateye's second top of the line below EL-530 as one piece unit runs on 4 AAs). My HL-1500 was brighter than EL-500. According to spec sheet, HL-1500(3000 candlepower) still brighter than EL-530(1500 candlepower). It still needs side by side comparison to be confirmed though. EL-530(also 500) has longer burn time(90 hrs advertized) and LED will last nearly forever, so it has some advantage. But it costs $60.- compare to $10.- +S/H for HL-1500.
For those of you maybe interested in getting HL-1500, Cambria bicycle outfitter(where I bought the first one) still sell them.

*update*(Jun-14-11)
The bulb seems to be very long lasting, specially compare to MicroHalogen bulb which in my guess was about 200 to 300 hours and I went through a few of them. I use HL-1500 regularly and the one of three I use most get used about a few hours a week but the original bulb is still working. Very dependable.

*update* (1-25-16)
My current light in use since 2012.
http://www.amazon.com/gp/review/R1BNGTL2ZIZ93D?ref_=glimp_1rv_cl
text_fidelity_b: Cateye HL-1500 Gray Silver Halogen Headlight

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Flex Wireless Activity + Sleep Wristband, Black, Pedometer, Small/Large I've had my Fitbit Flex for about a week. At first, I was fairly impressed when I actually counted my steps and compared it to the Fitbit calculations. However, it can be very quirky and inaccurate under certain circumstances. I have mine on my right wrist, and I am right-handed, so I made sure to set it to the "Dominant" wrist setting. But, to get truly accurate readings, your arm really needs to be at your side. If I'm carrying things around the house, I don't get an accurate count. If I'm walking through the store, pushing a grocery cart, I don't get an accurate count. It seriously under counts my steps. I'd like to send it back and exchange it for the Fitbit One, which I have since heard is more accurate. However, I didn't realize that Amazon only takes returns on unopened items, and otherwise charges a restocking fee. And, I'm not sure this is defective. I think it's just not accurate. Should have bought this from a Brick & Mortar store.

Edited 4/1/2014...Ok, I've been using my Fitbit for a few more days. Today I was out for several hours and my step count was still really low as, described previously, I don't walk with my hands down at my side. I'm usually busy doing other things. I had contacted Fitbit regarding the problem, but the only thing they could say was that it compared to other wrist-trackers on the market....which isn't saying a lot. I'd really like to return or exchange this thing, but can't. When I got home this afternoon, and saw that my step count was again very low, I decided to try taking the Flex unit out of the wrist band and I put it in my pocket. So far, that seems to give me a better step count. Not sure how it will work that way with the other functions. But, frankly, after using the Flex for over a week, I'm not confident in the accuracy of the other functions and will probably never use them. There is an Omron brand clip-on that gets rave reviews. Check that one out before you decide to buy the Flex.

Edited 4/3/2014...I pursued my issues with Fitbit customer service, and this is what they said: " Flex will count your steps when you're walking with your arms stationary, as we do want to give you credit for this activity. This includes walking while pushing a stroller or shopping cart, or holding on to a treadmill. However, because your hands are not moving, your step count may be a bit lower during this activity."

So, they have finally admitted the count is not accurate unless your arms are down at your side. I do dispute the fact that it is a "bit lower." My steps are hardly being counted at all, unless my arm is down at my side. So, for this reason, I have now lowered my rating to two stars. I did contact Amazon customer service and explained what was going on. They are allowing me to return it, without restocking charges, because it is not working as intended. THANKS AMAZON!!!
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Flex Wireless Activity + Sleep Wristband, Black, Pedometer, Small/Large

This has pros and cons over the simpler rings. On the pro side I can adjust the resistance of the grip, allowing me to progressively work my way from easier to harder exercises. On the con side a pair of these is a lot more expensive than the rings that I had been using.

After a week of using this on the minimum resistance setting (where I intend to keep it) the transition from the rings I was using to this was seamless. My normal exercises continued with no real changes to the routine, and this grip is not as easy to misplace as the rings.

Since I had been doing hand strength exercises for quite some time before using this device I can speak to the long term benefits of those (using any device). The strength such exercises develop and the working of muscles and joints are a hedge against the aging process because at sixty-six I was starting to feel the effects of age. Since my 'day job' is professional drummer my hands are important and this - and, to be fair, the rings I was using - keep my hands in shape. More importantly, they build strength and stamina.

Bottom line: this grip works, is well made, and can truly make a difference if you consistently use it.

text_fidelity_a:
Caboodles Tote I selected this bag to replace my laptop bag, which was taken by my college-age son when his previous bag failed him. My personal preference in bags is actually a messenger style bag, not a tote, so I wasn’t sure if this would be my new go-to bag or if I needed to keep shopping. It has proven to be a good bag and I am mostly happy with it.

This bag is large enough to handle a 15” laptop, but it is better suited for a smaller-sized laptop or tablet. It isn’t going to handle anything bigger, the limiting dimension being the height, unless you’re content with not zipping the bag or having the contents obstruct the handles. Of course there is room to put others things in the bag with said laptop too, so it’s not just a laptop sleeve.

The bag itself is made of a tight nylon weave with vinyl handles, a vinyl divider and an outside vinyl pocket. It is not impervious to cuts and nicks but the nylon is fine enough that it should resist most hazards such as desk corners. I looked this bag over very carefully and found no cuts, nicks or blemishes in the materials, the stitching is straight and there are no loose threads. Overall, it is made well.

If I could change two things...I would have used canvas instead of nylon which holds up better to frequent use and tends to be stronger. Time will tell if this bag will withstand steady use, but so far it’s faring well enough and showing no signs of fatigue. Also, I would have reinforced the bottom with a heavier material which is the one place where this bag seems most likely to eventually fail.

My preference in bags is still a messenger bag; that said, this is a decent bag that seems to be made well and is large enough to handle my laptop. If you prefer a tote bag to either a messenger or backpack, this one is worth consideration.
text_fidelity_b: Caboodles Tote

45 Degree Latitude 40 oz Water Bottle - Stay Hydrated Camping, Gym, Office Or Sports No BPA Stainless Steel Bottle - Perfectly Ice Cold Or Hot Beverages Leak Proof Lid - Perfect Gift - Celeste Green I wanted a larger water bottle for use at my workplace because I found that I was running low on water too often and was too busy (or, admittedly, too lazy) to take the 2 minute walk to refill my water bottle, leaving myself thirsty and dehydrated at my desk for hours. In doing my research for a worthy substitute, I was really attracted to this water bottle. I loved the company's sustainable values and how well-made their product seemed.

When I received the water bottle, I was surprised how lightweight on it is on its own; of course, it gets heavy when you fill it with 40 oz of water, which I wish that I had the foresight to realize before I made this purchase. It is so heavy and wide that I need to use two hands to pick up and drink out of when it is full. The other noticeable thing about the bottle is its beautiful color. I bought it in aqua and it is so eye-catching that I got two compliments on it in my small office during its first day of use.

I did not like the style of the cap which the water bottle came with, so after doing research, I purchased another brand's water bottle cap which was HydroFlask-compatible, which I also thought should be compatible with this one. Unfortunately, it is not. The cap screws on, but it leaks. Of course, this is not the fault of the brand or the water bottle, but it was disappointing to me, and if you are considering buying the bottle and swapping out the cap, this might be worth taking note of.

When I first bought this water bottle, I intended to use it all the time to replace my current water bottle. However, due to its hefty size and weight, I have decided to keep this bottle strictly at the office, as it is even too heavy and unwieldy to bring back and forth to my car, gym, and/or home. I drive a little sedan and it does not fit in my cup holders. I might be bringing it to the gym on my heavy cardio evenings, but it definitely staying in the office for pilates and barre. And it is definitely useful to have around for camping or hiking!

Overall great water bottle and very pleased with the product; unsure how practical it is for daily hydration use when commuting (unless you commute with a backpack).
text_fidelity_b: 45 Degree Latitude 40 oz Water Bottle - Stay Hydrated Camping, Gym, Office Or Sports No BPA Stainless Steel Bottle - Perfectly Ice Cold Or Hot Beverages Leak Proof Lid - Perfect Gift - Celeste Green

text_fidelity_a:
Portable Camping Water Purifier Dual 0.01 Micron Water Filtration System for Outdoor Backpacking, Hiking, Emergency - Dual Filters Version My son is the gizmo kid. He is always coming home with some sort of set up to try out some new intricate system whether it be electronics or board game development or survival gear. When he was starting to come home and excitedly show me his solar panels, battery collection devices for long term storage and charging and all of his plans to create a little camping area, I knew this would be great for him.

CHARGING
This does have to be charged, but knowing that he already had rigged up some sort of charging world with his solar panels and battery storage I did not think it would be a problem for him- which it isn't. He already explained a few ways to charge it in his system.

DOES IT WORK?
Getting details out of my son is not an easy feat. However, this works well, tastes good, and if you are prepared to wash it out now and then if you use really dirty water, you can keep it running well.

TASTE
He prefers not to use really muddy water, so that test is not one that really matters to him, but having water from a nearby pond or stream where he camps from time to time works well for this. The taste is good and he is happy.

IS IT HARD TO USE?
If this was too hard to use, he would not be using it. I would say that this is pretty straightforward and not difficult. You just have to air it out in between uses if you are not regularly running it.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This water purification system is great for camping or emergencies, as long as you have battery back up to charge it from if there is no power.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This has worked well for what my son wants it for and he seems happy with it. If we ever do need to use it in an emergency situation, I could try to update, but at that point, internet most likely won't be working anyway. LOL.
text_fidelity_b: Portable Camping Water Purifier Dual 0.01 Micron Water Filtration System for Outdoor Backpacking, Hiking, Emergency - Dual Filters Version
